title: Short QQQ — STEP ASIDE Macro Hedge: AI Dead Zone + Hormuz August CPI Loading
entry: Short $695–$718 at the July 17 open. NQ futures were down -1.9% premarket on July 17, placing QQQ at approximately $700–$704 at open. The entry zone ($695–$718) captures both the gap-down open and any intraday bounce that recovers toward $715–$718 before the STEP ASIDE macro dynamic reasserts. Do NOT short below $690 — at that level a technical oversold bounce is likely that would temporarily overwhelm the structural thesis. Do NOT initiate above $720 — above that level the Hormuz/AI dead zone setup is partially priced and the R:R compresses ahead of any bounce.
stop_loss: $738 daily close (~4.8% above $705 reference price) — implies (1) Iran ceasefire announced with Hormuz commercially re-opened above 70% of normal capacity, removing the Brent supply premium and August CPI loading thesis; OR (2) unexpected positive AI catalyst interrupts the 5-week dead zone (NVDA preannouncement of Q2 FY27 guidance above consensus, major hyperscaler intra-quarter capex raise above current consensus); OR (3) June core PCE (July 25) prints ≤-0.1% MoM (full disinflation confirmation collapsing September hike probability below 20% and triggering a broad Nasdaq risk-on). Above $738, the STEP ASIDE regime is structurally invalidated.
targets: $681 — SPX breaks and closes below the 7,460 support level flagged in the July 17 morning briefing; QQQ follows NQ to the 7,400–7,420 NQ zone; AI position-clearing spreads from semiconductor hardware (SMH) to semiconductor-dependent software (cloud AI names); hyperscaler earnings (July 29–30) add uncertainty premium ahead of their reports; +3.3% short gain from $705; cover 40%

risk_reward: 1:2.3 to Target 3 from $705 reference (risk $33; T3 reward $75)
catalyst: The July 17 morning briefing issued STEP ASIDE at HIGH conviction — the most restrictive regime signal in the daily framework, reserved for conditions where multiple concurrent macro risks outweigh the expected return from active long exposure. Three concurrent macro pressures are loading simultaneously: (1) AI position-clearing phase: NVDA -10.5% cumulative, TSMC Taipei -7.3%, SMH premarket -3.4% — not a correction but an institutional distribution event with no positive AI earnings catalyst until NVDA Q2 FY27 (August 26). (2) Hormuz-driven August CPI loading: Brent at $85.95 on July 17 will mechanically embed 0.8–1.2 percentage points of energy contribution into the August CPI print (released August 12). The August CPI is the last major inflation data point before the September 16–17 FOMC meeting, making it the deciding factor for whether September is a hike or a pause. (3) Iran conflict escalation beyond the blockade stage: US struck an Iranian oil tanker at Tehran's main export terminal; Iran retaliated on US bases in Kuwait and Jordan. This is kinetic escalation beyond Hormuz posturing, and it expands the geopolitical risk premium across Nasdaq's growth-multiple exposure.
thesis:
QQQ is the highest-liquid vehicle for expressing the STEP ASIDE regime at the macro level. It aggregates the AI semiconductor position-clearing (through NVDA, AMD, AVGO, QCOM in the top 10), the AI software uncertainty (MSFT, META, GOOGL, AMZN ahead of July 29–30 earnings), and the growth-multiple rate sensitivity (55%+ of QQQ is in rate-sensitive mega-cap tech). A single short on QQQ captures all three vectors without single-stock idiosyncratic risk.

The AI dead zone is the timing mechanism. Between today (July 17) and NVDA Q2 FY27 (August 26), there is no positive AI hardware earnings catalyst. The only scheduled events are: SPX/Nasdaq-100 quarterly rebalancing (July 22), FOMC (July 28–29), initial jobless claims (weekly), and hyperscaler earnings (META July 29, MSFT July 30, GOOGL July 29, AMZN July 30). Of these, the FOMC is the highest-impact event — but given September hike probability at 44.5% and Brent at $85.95, the FOMC is more likely to be hawkishly neutral than dovishly constructive. Hyperscaler earnings could be a positive catalyst if AI capex guidance is raised, but the IBM enterprise collapse (July 14) and TSMC wafer cost hike signal together suggest the AI capex acceleration narrative is more complex than simple 'raise guidance' extrapolation.

The 30Y at 5.097% — sixth consecutive session above 5.00% — is the valuation ceiling. Nasdaq-100 growth names are duration-sensitive assets. At 30Y 5.10%, the discount rate applied to 2027–2030 free cash flows for MSFT, GOOGL, and AMZN is materially higher than the consensus embedded in current forward P/E multiples. If the 30Y breaks 5.20% on August CPI loading, the multiple compression would be the dominant driver of QQQ downside — not an earnings miss, but a re-rating of existing estimates at higher discount rates.

This is a hedge position, not a structural bear call. The STEP ASIDE regime is not a 'market crash' prediction — it is a 'reduce gross exposure and hedge existing longs' instruction. QQQ short at 2% position size provides meaningful downside protection to the long book (XLE, XOM, ITA, USO, JPM) if a macro risk event triggers simultaneous broad selling. If the FOMC is neutral and Brent recovers toward $79 on any diplomatic signal, exit the QQQ short at the $738 stop and return to selective long mode. The counter-party is the Nasdaq bull who notes that CPI and PPI have both printed favorably (0.0% MoM core CPI, -0.3% PPI), and that rate-cut expectations for September are meaningful (44.5% probability of a pause rather than hike). This bull is correct that the inflation data is constructive; the STEP ASIDE signal acknowledges this by labeling the regime as 'selective' rather than 'avoid all longs.' The QQQ short exists to hedge the portfolio against the scenario where the Hormuz tail risk proves larger than the favorable CPI/PPI signal.
bull_case: Iran-US ceasefire announced July 19–20; Brent collapses from $85.95 to $73–75; September hike probability falls from 44.5% to 25% on the same day; 30Y breaks below 4.80%. QQQ gaps up 3–4% to $728–$732. Exit the short before the $738 stop is triggered. Simultaneously, hyperscaler earnings July 29–30 all raise AI capex guidance. STEP ASIDE regime ends by July 21 on diplomatic de-escalation.
bear_case: Iran conflict escalates further with power plant strikes (Trump threat from July 17 briefing); Brent pushes above $90; August CPI loading becomes severe (0.9+ percentage points of energy contribution); September hike probability hits 65%+; 30Y tests 5.20%. QQQ falls from $705 toward $658 (T2) by July 28 ahead of FOMC. FOMC holds rates but statement is explicitly hawkish ('prepared to act'). QQQ tests $630 (T3) ahead of NVDA Q2 FY27 in August.
invalidation: $738 QQQ daily close; OR Iran ceasefire announced with Hormuz commercially re-opened above 70% capacity (WTI falls below $70 immediately — Brent supply premium evaporates); OR June PCE (July 25) ≤3.0% MoM-annualized (full disinflation confirmation removing the September hike scenario entirely); OR all four hyperscalers (META, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN) collectively raise FY2026 AI capex guidance 15%+ above consensus at July 29–30 earnings (positive AI catalyst interrupts dead zone); OR NVDA issues explicit positive preannouncement before August 26 raising Q2 FY27 revenue guidance above $52B
